title: Fjord Energy predictive-maintenance inference eval and runbook
content:
Summary:

This note captures the benchmarking methodology, observed performance, cost projection, and an operational runbook for the Fjord Energy predictive-maintenance POC. Goal: determine a production topology that meets a 300ms p95 inference SLO for short-form telemetry summaries (avg output: 120 tokens) while minimizing per-inference cost.

Context and constraints:
- Workload: time-series+metadata -> prompt construction -> model summarization + anomaly classification. Typical request payload ~1.2k characters.
- SLO target: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 450ms.
- Expected QPS: baseline 15 sustained, peak 70 QPS bursts (10s windows).
- Data sensitivity: customer prefers Dedicated with VPC; initial POC runs on hosted dedicated GPUs.
- Models tested: redwood-alpha-3b (float16), redwood-alpha-7b-q4_0 (4-bit quant), llama-3-13b-8k (float16) as a compatibility baseline.

Test matrix and environment:
- Hardware: H100 80GB (dedicated), A100 80GB (baseline), L4 for small-embedding fallback.
- Serving runtime: Redwood inference runtime v2.4.1 with continuous batching enabled and prefix KV cache on for repeated metadata queries.
- Configs varied: concurrency (1, 2, 4), max_batch_size (1, 8, 16), kv_cache_enabled (on/off), quantization (float16 vs q4_0).
- Synthetic load: Poisson arrival to simulate burstiness; also replayed 48-hour production trace sample provided by Fjord (sanitized).
- Measurement method: 10 full runs per configuration; collect p50/p95/p99, tail latency distribution, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and estimated cost per 1M requests.

Key findings (high level):
1) Best trade-off for SLO+cost: redwood-alpha-7b-q4_0 on H100 with concurrency=2 and max_batch_size=8. Observed p95: 280ms, p99: 420ms, throughput 55 qps sustained.
2) Float16 3B is cheaper but p95 variability high under bursts due to inefficient KV cache utilization for our prompt patterns (p95 ~360–420ms at 50 QPS).
3) Llama-3-13b exceeded memory budget for burst batching (cold-started KV cache blowup) and required higher instance sizing; not recommended for Dedicated cost targets.
4) Enabling KV cache reduced median token compute by ~18% and improved tail latencies substantially for requests with repeated metadata.
5) Quantized 7B reduced GPU memory pressure and allowed larger effective batch sizes with lower cost-per-token while preserving output quality for this workload (manual evaluation: 92% parity with float16 baseline).

Representative numbers (H100, production trace, mean output 120 tokens):
- redwood-alpha-7b-q4_0 (concurrency=2, batch=8): p50 95ms, p95 280ms, p99 420ms, sustain throughput 55 qps, GPU util 68%, est cost per 1M requests: $1,750.
- redwood-alpha-3b fp16 (concurrency=4, batch=16): p50 65ms, p95 380ms, p99 620ms, sustain throughput 70 qps, GPU util 82%, est cost per 1M requests: $1,120 (but higher SLA risk).
- llama-3-13b fp16 (concurrency=1, batch=4): p50 180ms, p95 520ms, p99 900ms, sustain throughput 18 qps, est cost per 1M requests: $3,400.

Cost assumptions used:
- GPU runtime price: H100 $6.00/hr (internal committed rate), A100 $4.25/hr, L4 $1.10/hr (equivalent instance cost used for per-token).
- Average GPU tokens/sec measured extrapolated to per-hour token capacity.
- Overhead: 8% added for networking and infra overhead, 12% for reserved capacity idle time factoring burst headroom.

Operational observations and edge cases:
- Cold-start microbursts: cold KV cache ~+120ms tail observed for long-tailed requests. Mitigation: warm-up policy (maintain a small pinned warm pool during anticipated load windows, or keep a tiny warm instance per region).
- Tokenization overhead: telemetry preprocessing in Python (server-side) added 30–60ms for longer prompts; moving tokenization into a Rust microservice reduced median by ~22ms and improved tail. Consider shipping a compiled tokenization binary as a sidecar.
- Batch amplification risk: for short outputs (<=40 tokens) batching improves GPU efficiency, but for outputs near 120 tokens batching beyond 16 created p99 amplification; tune max_batch_size per model.
- Network variance: multi-region routing added jitter (~20–40ms) — for strict SLO prefer regional routing and fallbacks.

Quality check (human eval):
- 250 random samples compared between float16 3B and q4_0 7B: semantic parity score 0.92 (precision/recall-like scoring based on domain labels and summary fidelity). False-positive anomaly rate slightly higher on 7B-q4_0 (1.8% vs 1.2%) — acceptable per Fjord product team for initial deploy.

Recommended production topology (phase 1):
- Primary: Dedicated H100 pool running redwood-alpha-7b-q4_0, concurrency=2, max_batch_size=8, KV cache on. Scale: reserve capacity sized for 60 QPS sustained with autoscale to absorb 80 QPS peaks.
- Warm standby: 1 small A100 instance running alpha-3b-fp16 for fast lightweight fallbacks under overload, with auto-failover routing policy.
- Edge routing: regional deployment in us-west1 and eu-west1; latency-aware routing + capacity-based fallback.
- Observability: enable per-token latency breakdown, batch size distribution histograms, and per-request KV cache hit tag. Create a dashboard tile for cold-start rate.

Runbook: (actions for SRE and SE during rollout)
1) Pre-launch: run a 12-hour soak at 0.8x expected traffic to verify mem-pressure patterns and cache warm rates. Log p95/p99 and GPU OOM events.
2) Warm policy: deploy a policy to keep 2 pinned warm replicas per region between 07:00–20:00 local time.
3) Canary rollout: start with 5% traffic for 2 hours, verify p95 <= 300ms and no quality regressions on a sampled prompt set. If p95 spikes > 350ms or regression rate > 2% for more than 15 minutes, abort and rollback.
4) Autoscale policy: scale based on queue depth + observed batch formation time. Hard cap on concurrency 4 to avoid CPU serialization overhead.
5) Incident playbook: on p95 breach, engage the following sequence: (a) throttle ingress to 60% of baseline, (b) enable fallback routing to alpha-3b pool, (c) add warm instances, (d) contact SE lead.

Next steps and open questions:
- Run a quality-focused A/B with 10k production-like requests comparing 7B-q4_0 vs 3B-fp16 to confirm parity across edge cases.
- Evaluate further quantization modes (q5_x) once runtime support lands in v2.5.
- Confirm reserved capacity pricing with infra finance for H100 burst credits.
- Follow up on tokenization sidecar rollout: target performance PR by 2028-03-18.

Appendix: quick reference commands and artifacts
- Load harness: github.com/redwood-inference/fjord-poc (bin/loadgen --trace fjord_trace.json --model redwood-alpha-7b-q4_0 --concurrency 2 --batch 8)
- Linear ticket for rollout: FJ-92 (linked above)
- Suggested dashboard tiles: p95-latency-per-model, batch-size-distribution, kv-cache-hit-rate, cold-start-rate

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a tiny LRU prefix cache in front of model for repeated metadata prompts to further shave tail.
- Investigate offloading tokenization to a dedicated pinned CPU thread group to avoid Python GIL stalls during bursts.

Prepared by: Ava Chen (SE lead)
Reviewed: Diego Morales, Priya Nair
